chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:
About the sacrificial animal: if the one slaughtering it makes a mistake and mentions someone other than its owner, does it suffice on behalf of the owner of the sacrifice?
He said: “Yes. One only has what he intended.”

key_terms.أَتُجْزِي: does it suffice or count as valid
key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the sacrificial offering made on the occasion of Eid al-Adha
key_terms.يُخْطِئُ: makes a mistake or errs unintentionally

ai.seo_question: If the slaughterer mistakenly names the wrong person during an udhiyah, is the sacrifice still valid for its owner?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the udhiyah sacrifice. If the slaughterer mistakenly names someone other than the owner, the sacrifice is still valid for the one whose intention it was, showing that legal consideration here follows intention rather than an accidental verbal error.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3065 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) about a sacrificial animal:
if the one slaughtering it mistakenly mentions a name other than its owner, does it suffice for the owner of the sacrifice?
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, it is for the one who intended it."
